newsitem.title: INDIA: Voting staggered in India's Uttar Pradesh state.
newsitem.headline: Voting staggered in India's Uttar Pradesh state.

text.p: Elections to the local assembly in India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, began on Monday with voting in 135 of 425 constituencies.

Two more days of voting will be held on October 3 and 7 in the remaining constituencies. The polling is staggered to allow thousands of election officials and security forces time to move across the state from west to east.
Bounded in the north by the Himalayan mountains and bisected by the Ganges river, Uttar Pradesh has 140 million people and some 100 million eligible voters.

In Monday's polling, 33 million voters were eligible to choose from among 1,830 candidates. Nearly 40,000 polling stations were set up across the western third of the state, which is bigger than France in area.
Tens of thousands of paramilitary troops have been deployed along with police.
A total of more than 12,000 polling stations have been identified as "hyper-sensitive", requiring extra security in a state long known for its violent politics.
Vote counting will begin after the third day of polling on October 7, and final results are expected by mid-month.
